grammar_choice.en_template: Fashion is always deeply cultural, and an excellent example of this can {{1:be seen/see}} in the evolution of European {{2:clothing/clothe}}.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 패션은 항상 문화와 깊이 연결되어 있으며, 이에 대한 훌륭한 예시를 유럽 복식의 변천 과정에서 찾아볼 수 있다.
explain: can + 수동태 → be seen(찾아볼 수 있다).
명사 자리 → clothing(의복). clothe는 동사.

grammar_choice.en_template: At the beginning of the Middle Ages, clothing tended {{1:to be/being}} simple and was frequently made {{2:of/from}} rough wool or animal furs.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 중세 초기에 의복은 단순한 경향이 있었고, 거친 양모나 동물 모피로 자주 만들어졌다.
explain: tend to + 동사원형 → to be.
재료를 나타낼 때 원형이 유지되면 made of; made of rough wool(원형 재료 유지) → of.

grammar_choice.en_template: With advances in cloth making, however, fashion began moving toward styles {{1:that/what}} were more elaborate and form-fitting.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 그러나 직물 제조의 발전에 따라 패션은 더 정교하고 몸에 딱 맞는 스타일로 이동하기 시작했다.
explain: 선행사 styles가 있으므로 관계대명사는 that 또는 which. what은 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사이므로 선행사 뒤에 쓸 수 없다 — that이 정답.

grammar_choice.en_template: In the Renaissance and Elizabethan eras, styles {{1:became/become}} even {{2:more refined/most refined}}.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 르네상스와 엘리자베스 시대에는 스타일이 한층 더 세련되어졌다.
explain: 과거 시제 서술 → became.
even + 비교급 강조 → more refined(비교급). most refined는 최상급.

grammar_choice.en_template: The clothes {{1:that/which}} wealthy people were wearing became increasingly fancier, with a particular emphasis {{2:being placed/to place}} on smaller waists.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 부유한 사람들이 입는 옷은 점점 더 화려해졌으며, 특히 더 가는 허리에 강조점이 놓였다.
explain: 선행사 The clothes를 수식하는 관계사절 — that(또는 which) 모두 가능; that.
with + 명사 + 분사 구문: emphasis가 놓이는 대상 → 수동 현재분사 being placed.

grammar_choice.en_template: The connection between clothing and social status was so {{1:pronounced/pronouncing}} that laws were {{2:enacted/enacting}} to limit the wearing of certain luxury items.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 의복과 사회적 지위 사이의 연관성은 너무나 뚜렷하여 특정 사치품의 착용을 제한하는 법률이 제정되었다.
explain: 서술적 형용사 자리 → pronounced(뚜렷한). pronouncing은 현재분사·동명사.
laws가 제정되는 대상 → 수동태 were enacted.

grammar_choice.en_template: {{1:Allowed/Allowing}} only for higher social classes, luxurious styles and decorations such as feathers, silk, or velvet {{2:were used/used}} as a means of demonstrating one's standing in society.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 높은 사회 계층에게만 허용된 화려한 스타일과 장식들은 사회에서 자신의 위치를 과시하는 수단으로 사용되었다.
explain: 주어 luxurious styles가 허용을 받는 대상 → 수동 분사구문 Allowed.
주어가 사용된 것이므로 수동태 were used.

grammar_choice.en_template: This was further reinforced as upperclass styles came {{1:to be/being}} explicitly incorporated into cultural ceremonies so that their wearers' roles could be {{2:identified/identifying}} clearly.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 이는 상류층의 스타일이 문화적 의식에 명시적으로 통합되어 참여자들의 역할이 명확하게 식별될 수 있게 됨에 따라 더욱 강화되었다.
explain: come to + 동사원형 → to be (come to be incorporated = 통합되게 되다).
wearers' roles가 식별되는 대상 → 수동태 be identified.

explain: '문화와 깊이 연결됨' — cultural(문화적인). natural은 문맥과 반대.
변천·발전의 역사 → evolution(변천). regression(퇴보)은 반대말.

vocab_choice.en_template: At the beginning of the Middle Ages, clothing tended to be {{1:simple/ornate}} and was {{2:frequently/rarely}} made of rough wool or animal furs.

explain: 중세 초기의 소박한 복식 → simple(단순한). ornate(화려한)는 이후 시대에 해당.

vocab_choice.en_template: With advances in cloth making, however, fashion began moving toward styles that were more {{1:elaborate/crude}} and {{2:form-fitting/loose}}.

explain: 발전 후 더 '정교한' 스타일 → elaborate. crude(조잡한)는 발전 이전.
'몸에 딱 맞는' — form-fitting. loose(헐렁한)는 반대말.

explain: 점점 더 '세련되어진' — refined(세련된). coarse(거친)는 앞 시대에 해당하는 반대말.

vocab_choice.en_template: The clothes that wealthy people were wearing became {{1:increasingly/decreasingly}} fancier, with a particular {{2:emphasis/neglect}} being placed on smaller waists.

jumble.answer: Fashion is always deeply cultural, and an excellent example of this can be seen in the evolution of European clothing.
At the beginning of the Middle Ages, clothing tended to be simple and was frequently made of rough wool or animal furs.
With advances in cloth making, however, fashion began moving toward styles that were more elaborate and form-fitting.
In the Renaissance and Elizabethan eras, styles became even more refined.
The clothes that wealthy people were wearing became increasingly fancier, with a particular emphasis being placed on smaller waists.
The connection between clothing and social status was so pronounced that laws were enacted to limit the wearing of certain luxury items.
Allowed only for higher social classes, luxurious styles and decorations such as feathers, silk, or velvet were used as a means of demonstrating one's standing in society.
This was further reinforced as upperclass styles came to be explicitly incorporated into cultural ceremonies so that their wearers' roles could be identified clearly.
